reason: DNA nucleotides are the building blocks needed to copy the DNA shown in the nucleus.
expectation: The nucleotides will be used to copy the genome.

alternatives.reason: These are the visible components for building the spindle.

effect: The genome is copied, leaving membrane growth and spindle construction as the current goals.
reaction: The distinction between copying the whole genome and making proteins is useful.
reason: The centrosomes organize microtubules, and the tubulin and motors are the visible spindle components.
expectation: These components will form a chromosome-separating spindle.

alternatives.reason: Phospholipids may help build the growing cell's membrane.

effect: The spindle is built, and making daughter cells is now a goal; membrane growth remains unfinished.
reaction: The spindle image makes clear that building it and separating chromosomes are distinct steps.
reason: Phospholipids are the visible membrane-building material, and the cell needs more membrane as it grows.
expectation: The phospholipids will contribute to membrane growth.

effect: The attempted cell combination instead revealed that phospholipids and proteins make membrane vesicles; growing the surface and contents is now the goal.
reaction: The vesicles clarify that membrane components are assembled before being added to the cell.
reason: The new vesicles appear to supply membrane for the living cell's growing surface.
expectation: The vesicles will contribute membrane to the growing cell.

effect: The vesicles fused with the cell surface, completing growth; the remaining goal is to make daughter cells with complete genomes.
reaction: The before-and-after view usefully connects membrane expansion with growth of the cell's contents.
reason: The copied genome and mitotic spindle are the components needed to separate chromosomes before division.
expectation: The spindle will help separate the copied chromosomes.

effect: The spindle has separated the chromosome copies, but the cell still needs its cytoplasm divided.
reaction: The distinction between chromosome separation and forming two cells is clear.
reason: The separated chromosome sets must be brought together with the grown cell body before it can divide.
expectation: This will bring the separated genomes into the grown-cell division sequence.

alternatives.reason: Actin and myosin could help divide the cell's cytoplasm.

effect: The separated chromosome sets now have daughter nuclei, but both remain in one shared cytoplasm.
reaction: The new nuclear envelopes make the remaining division of the cell body clear.
reason: Cortical actin and myosin can contract beneath the membrane to divide the shared cytoplasm.

choice.with: Stem cell with two daughter nuclei

expectation: Actin and myosin will help split the cell into two daughter stem cells.

effect: Actin and myosin completed division into two unspecialized daughter stem cells, each with a complete genome; all goals are complete.
reaction: It was satisfying to see chromosome separation and cytoplasmic division come together as distinct stages.

mostWorthwhile.text: Separating the copied chromosomes and then forming daughter nuclei was most worthwhile: the picture descriptions distinguish genome distribution from division of the shared cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: Building the spindle was relatively thin as a passage: the picture shows fibres, but the accompanying wonder adds no explanation of how they attach to and move chromosomes.

surprise.text: I expected phospholipids to go directly into the cell, but compatibility feedback led instead to membrane vesicles made with proteins; those subsequently fused with the surface.

arbitrary.text: Combining the separated chromosome sets with the enlarged cell body felt somewhat like merging two views of the same cell rather than a physical action, although it led to a clear daughter-nuclei picture.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: connecting the separate chromosome and cell-body views made the division sequence interesting, and the descendants taking different paths suggest a useful next question about specialization.
